When Starlink helped save five lives at sea.

A boat called Magic Bus was sinking in a storm, far off the coast of North Carolina.

The captain tried to call for help using the boat’s radio, but couldn’t reach anyone. He then used @Starlink Mini to connect his phone and call the U.S. Coast Guard.

The five people left the sinking boat in a liferaft. Rescuers arrived by helicopter and brought everyone back safely. Starlink helped them reach help when their lives were in danger.

This life-saving technology should be available in every part of the world.

A Tennessee truck driver named Tony Alsup didn’t wait for official rescue teams when Hurricane Florence bore down on the Carolinas in 2018. 

He bought a used school bus, stripped out every seat, and pointed it straight at the storm.

He called the stripped-down bus Noah’s Ark. Inside it, he loaded 53 dogs and 11 cats—64 animals in all—taken from overcrowded shelters that stood in the path of rising floodwaters. 

He deliberately chose the ones most shelters struggle to place: older dogs, animals with medical conditions, and the “leftovers” that often get left behind when space runs out. 

Cages stacked along the walls, blankets spread across the floor, and dogs standing on the seats he had left in place turned the bus into a rolling kennel.

Alsup drove the animals out of the danger zone and delivered them safely to a receiving shelter in Foley, Alabama. 

From there they were dispersed to facilities across the country that still had room. He covered the fuel costs himself. The trip was not a one-off. After earlier storms—Harvey, Irma, and Maria—he had already begun hauling supplies into disaster areas and pulling shelter animals out of them. 

Florence simply gave him a larger vehicle and a clearer target.

The image of Alsup sitting in the driver’s seat of that bus, dogs peering over seat backs and carriers lining the aisle, captures the scale of what one person decided was possible when the water started rising. 

The animals reached dry ground. Most of them eventually found homes. The bus, for a few critical days, did exactly what he built it to do. ❤️🐾

The song and the movie that took the nation by storm.
Jai Santoshi Maa , 1975
The song and film turned cinema halls into impromptu temples, where audiences would remove their shoes, light diyas  and sing along.
It has since become a staple devotional track, frequently played during Navratri and Dandiya nights.
The song was beautifully voiced by Usha Mangeshkar.
The simple yet deeply poetic lyrics were penned by Kavi Pradeep, a celebrated patriotic and devotional poet of India.
Music C. Arjun 
The film was made on a tiny shoestring budget of just ₹3 Lakhs, but went on to make history by beating massive blockbusters like Sholay in terms of return on investment (ROI).
